metric_rationale: In Trial 3 and Trial 4, Tallying sees exactly equal feature wins for A and B, so it predicts a 50/50 guess regardless of its temperature parameter. WADD, on the other hand, evaluates the weighted sum of validities, which will rarely balance out exactly, leading to a systematic preference for one option over the other. By calculating the absolute deviation of the choice probability from 0.5 on these specific trials for each subject, we can distinctly separate Tallying (low deviation, driven only by binomial sampling noise) from WADD (high deviation, driven by systematic preference).

This metric isolates trials where Tallying and WADD have completely opposite strict preferences. Specifically, it looks at trials where one option has fewer positive features (2 vs 3) but those features include the most highly predictive ones (e.g., the feature at index 0). Tallying will strictly prefer the option with 3 features (yielding a metric near 0), whereas WADD will strictly prefer the option with 2 features because of their high validity (yielding a metric near 1).
